A.title: Offer every young jobless person a real placement fast, with a fair duty
A.answer: What changes: the existing Jobs Guarantee, a fully funded six-month job, opens for under-25s after three months on Universal Credit instead of the planned 12, paid at least the legal wage. Taking a suitable offer becomes the condition of continued support, but nobody who is sick or disabled is sanctioned. Who does it: the Work and Pensions Secretary, paid for by moving money from the 2.5 billion pound Youth Guarantee and the spending on the consequences of inactivity (25 pounds for every 1 pound on opportunity), with no new tax. How we'd know: the Youth Opportunities Unit publishes quarterly, by area, how many take up offers, how many reach lasting work, and what each cost. [s1][s2]

B.title: Give each area's youth guarantee to a local board that holds the money
B.answer: The government would not keep this in a Prime Minister-facing Unit [s1]; it would hand the existing 2.5 billion pound Youth Guarantee [s2] to local boards, one per area, run by the council, the college and local employers. Each board would also hold the Jobs Guarantee places [s2]. The Unit would audit and publish results, not run services. How we would know: after a year, compare each area's count of young people not in education, employment or training with the national figure of close to a million [s1], and see whether the boards beat it. Citizens in the simulation backed only 6 votes for local control, so it needs proving.
